other_failure_modes.name: Data-dependent feature engineering applied independently
other_failure_modes.description: Applying conditional feature engineering (e.g., thresholding based on max values) independently to the train and test sets can result in inconsistent schemas (missing columns) or different transformations being applied if the test distribution differs slightly.

other_failure_modes.name: Improper handling of ID column
other_failure_modes.description: The agent fails to extract and drop the ID column from the datasets before training, meaning models might use it as a predictive feature and overfit. Furthermore, it hardcodes sequential IDs for the submission, which will fail if the true test IDs are non-sequential.

summary: The solution is generally robust, employing proper 10-fold cross-validation, extensive feature engineering, and a tuned ensemble of diverse models without leaking data. However, it applies data-dependent feature transformations independently to train and test sets (risking schema mismatches), and it fails to properly extract and preserve the test ID column for the submission file.
